business_problem: IBM's client-facing teams were losing time switching among disconnected sales, support and planning tools, leaving them without a timely, shared account view when preparing for customer interactions.
solution_summary: The IBM Chief Information Office organization built an Account 360 Slack application on its internal Hybrid Cloud platform to reduce the time client-facing teams spent hunting across disconnected sales, support and planning tools. The solution aligns account identifiers across source systems, combines quote documents, support tickets, account plans, company profiles and other client records, preprocesses them and stores the result in IBM Cloud Object Storage. The application is written in Python and hosted on Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud, while IBM watsonx.ai generates summaries and answers natural-language questions over the aggregated account material. Slack is the serving layer, exposing one-click access to relevant resources and teammates from desktop or mobile devices. This creates a cross-silo retrieval and collaboration layer where normalized account data is stored once and surfaced inside the tool where sellers, customer success managers and support staff already work.

data_flow: Sales, support and planning data is aligned by account identifier, combined and preprocessed into IBM Cloud Object Storage, then served by a Python application on OpenShift; Slack exposes the output while watsonx.ai summarizes account documents and answers account questions.
business_outcome: IBM deployed the pilot in 6-8 weeks, rolled it out to about 70 accounts, and gave account teams a faster way to get up to speed, coordinate with teammates and respond to client questions without manually stitching context together.
architecture_clues: The application was written in Python and hosted within IBM's internal Hybrid Cloud platform.
Preprocessed account data is stored before users make requests so responses can be served quickly.
The design depends on finding and linking common account identifiers across sales and support systems.
